scope: Source-compatible resolution of an mzML sourceFileRef that names no preceding definition, on a spectrum, a scan and a precursor (decision D14, wave 8), and the round trip it exists for: the streaming MSDataWritingConsumer under ReferencePolicy::SourceDangling writes the sf_sp_<s> the source writes, and the reader must take it back. Selected by the existing mzml::ReadOptions::source_dangling_references; the default stays strict. This reverses the 'sourceFileRef is out of scope and stays strict' line of work package P2-MZML-LENIENCY, deliberately, because the port had otherwise introduced a file only the C++ reader would read. A chromatogram's sourceFileRef is not covered: mzML 1.1 has no such attribute on ChromatogramType and the reader refuses it before any policy applies.

source_anchors.operation: spectrum sourceFileRef: `if (source_files_.contains(ref)) spec_.setSourceFile(source_files_[ref]); else OPENMS_LOG_WARN << "Error: unregistered source file reference " << ref` -- the record keeps the SourceFile() its fresh construction gave it, and nothing is inserted into the map
chromatogram sourceFileRef: chromatogram_.setSourceFile(source_files_[ref]); std::map::operator[] default-constructs AND inserts, silently
scan sourceFileRef: tmp.setMetaValue("source_file_name", source_files_[ref].getNameOfFile()) and the path beside it; both keys are set unconditionally, to empty strings for an unknown ID
spectrum precursor sourceFileRef, and at 1339 a chromatogram precursor's: the same two metaValues through operator[]

end of sourceFileList: source_files_ is copied into exp_->getSourceFiles(). This runs before the run element, so the record-time operator[] insertions never reach the experiment's source-file list -- measured: exp_source_files = 1 on a fixture naming two dangling IDs

writeSpectrum_: sourceFileRef="sf_sp_<s>" for every record after the first that carries a source file, and dataProcessingRef="dp_sp_<s>" when spec.getDataProcessing() != dps[0] -- a POINTER comparison over std::vector<std::shared_ptr<const DataProcessing>>
writeHeader_: dps is deduplicated by CONTENT with Helpers::cmpPtrContainer, which is why the whole-document writer dangles on content-equal, pointer-distinct histories (CPP-172)

fixtures.kind: synthetic, hand-written mzML 1.1: one declared sourceFile and five records covering the shapes -- a resolved spectrum reference, a dangling one, a dangling scan reference, a dangling precursor reference, and the first dangling ID named a second time so the per-occurrence/per-ID warning difference is visible
oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential): the lines of ../oracle/reader-roundtrip/logs/probe_06.log that the probe wrote for the three inputs, verbatim

external_reference_note: No C++ is committed to this repository. The probe, its build and the round-trip driver live in ../oracle/reader-roundtrip/ and link the unmodified Release install at the pins, /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/opt/openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576, on ibminode06. Only the probe's stdout and the two mzML inputs enter the repository, with the hashes above.
method: Oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential): probe_source_refs.cpp loads each input with MzMLFile::load and prints, per record, the SourceFile the reader ends up with, whether a scan's and a precursor's source_file_name/source_file_path metadata exist and what they hold, the experiment's own source-file list, and which records share one DataProcessing allocation. tests/mzml_source_file_round_trip.rs renders the Rust reader's results in the same line format, reading with source_dangling_references and AcquisitionMode::Source (the default Canonical mode collapses a lone empty scan, a separately documented native normalization that would otherwise enter this comparison), and requires all 52 lines to be equal. Round trip, executed both ways on ibminode06 by roundtrip_06.sh: both implementations write the refs, dupdp and 110-record FileMerger inputs in both -processOption modes, and every written file is read by BOTH implementations -- FileInfo for the exit code and the in-memory tool for a read-and-write-back whose decoded content is compared under rule D6. Tier 4 (Rust-only): the strict default refuses all three shapes, on the whole fixture and on each shape alone; one warning per distinct dangling ID per read and none for a strict read; the crate's own low-memory output of an input with per-record source files reads back with the peaks bit-identical; the whole-document writer's remaining content deduplication is pinned as a divergence.

target_verification.tests: tests/mzml_source_file_round_trip.rs (5), the updated tests/mzml_header_leniency.rs (8), tests/ms_data_writing_consumer.rs (36) and tests/topp_peak_picker_hi_res.rs (34), on stable and 1.85.0, under --all-features and under --no-default-features --features mzml,paramxml
target_verification.cpp_issue_candidate: Already recorded as CPP-172 and widened by wave 7: MzMLHandler::writeHeader_ deduplicates data-processing histories by content (Helpers::cmpPtrContainer) while writeSpectrum_ compares them by pointer, so both the streaming consumer and the whole-document MzMLFile::store emit dataProcessingRef and sourceFileRef values that no id declares, which mzML 1.1 forbids (xs:IDREF against xs:ID, plus KEYREF_DPREF). This group adds the measured reader side: the same MzMLHandler reads those files without failing, warning only for a spectrum's sourceFileRef and saying nothing for a chromatogram's, a scan's or a precursor's.
